mutants.why: Lossy normalization removes punctuation, so foo-bar and foobar share a key. lossyNormalizedKeyNeverAuthorizesSelection requires the sole foobar candidate to stay human-gated for query foo-bar while raw case-insensitive foo-bar still selects.
Silencing the surrounding-whitespace guard turns a padded id into another valid token after trim. rejectsUnsafePackageIdDomain requires the padded record to be rejected before selection.
Capping only trimmed input lets an arbitrarily large whitespace query bypass the work bound. rejectsOversizedRawQueryBeforeTrimming feeds limit+1 spaces and requires the too-long refusal.
Every present alias is attacker-controlled. boundsAndSanitizesCandidateMetadata requires an oversized title and an oversized whitespace description to be rejected before retention.

Copying the complete search object retains unlimited unknown metadata. boundsAndSanitizesCandidateMetadata supplies a 100000-character blob and requires it absent from both source and serialized candidate.
Returning after the first usable alias skips type validation of later present aliases. rejectsMalformedLaterAlias provides package_id=firefox plus numeric id=7 and requires the whole record rejected.

Forgetting the conflict falls back to generic exact-id ambiguity even though repeating the id cannot resolve contradictory versions. exposesConflictingDuplicateVersions requires explicit conflict text, no human exact-id question, and both versions visible.
A mixed valid/malformed response must not hide rejected records just because one candidate selected. reportsRejectedEntriesOnSuccessfulSelection requires rejected_entries=1 in the result and JSON.
